universities.name: University of Lisbon Faculty of Medicine
universities.summary: University of Lisbon Faculty of Medicine offers the six-year, 360-ECTS Integrated Master's in Medicine in Lisbon. For the verified 2026/27 international route, the Faculty publishes EUR 18,000 annual tuition, a EUR 100 application fee, Portuguese or English B1 entry evidence, an academic review and interview, and a Portuguese-language progression condition for applicants who enter without Portuguese B1.
universities.campusLifestyle: The Faculty is located in Lisbon and forms part of the University of Lisbon. Its published student information connects degree students with University services, while housing, food, transport and personal expenses sit outside the Medicine tuition published for international admission.
universities.cityProfile: Lisbon is the programme city. University of Lisbon practical information publishes indicative city costs for meals, rooms, studios and public transport, while actual housing depends on location and contract terms. The University operates student residences and its social-support services manage accommodation applications, but availability and monthly charges are separate from the Faculty's Medicine tuition. This package therefore treats housing as a planning item rather than an included benefit.
universities.practicalExposure: The Faculty's history places it with the Hospital de Santa Maria from 1953. Its director describes the Faculty, GIMM and ULS Santa Maria as part of the Centro Académico de Medicina de Lisboa, a clinical academic centre. The official Integrated Master's description confirms a 12-semester, 360-ECTS route, with the first three years constituting the 180-ECTS basic medical-studies cycle and the full degree awarded after completion of the final Integrated Master's work. This package does not turn those institutional links into a named clinical-placement guarantee.
universities.hostelOverview: University of Lisbon publishes student halls of residence and states that monthly fees are set annually. Its current student guide says applications are available to degree students, with priority for scholarship holders from outside Lisbon; room assignment and price are not included in this Medicine package.
universities.dietarySupport: University of Lisbon practical information lists an indicative monthly meals cost for Lisbon, but the Faculty does not publish a Medicine meal plan as part of the verified tuition route. Food remains a separate personal cost.
universities.safetyOverview: No Faculty-specific safety statistic was verified for this package. The University provides arrival, visa and practical-information guidance for international students, while accommodation and travel arrangements remain personal responsibilities.
universities.studentSupport: University of Lisbon student guidance describes access to social-support services, residences, sports, health and well-being services, digital tools and dining halls. These University-wide services are distinct from a guaranteed Faculty accommodation, scholarship or clinical placement.

faq.question: How long is Medicine at the University of Lisbon Faculty of Medicine?
faq.answer: The Integrated Master's in Medicine lasts 12 semesters and carries 360 ECTS. The first three years form the 180-ECTS basic medical-studies cycle, and the full degree follows completion of the programme and final Integrated Master's work.

faq.question: What is the published 2026/27 international tuition?
faq.answer: The Faculty's international-Medicine page publishes EUR 18,000 per year. The EUR 108,000 six-year figure is a calculation from that annual tuition, not an all-inclusive Faculty package.

faq.question: Is Medicine taught fully in English?
faq.answer: No. The international page accepts Portuguese or English B1 evidence at entry. Applicants entering without Portuguese B1 are required to complete Portuguese study by the end of the third year, so this is not presented as a fully English-medium route.

faq.question: Who can use the international-student Medicine route?
faq.answer: The 2026/27 call is for applicants who meet Portugal's international-student definition and hold a qualification giving higher-education access in their education system, or the relevant Portuguese secondary qualification. EU citizens and several resident or family categories are excluded from that route.

faq.question: How are applicants selected?
faq.answer: For the verified 2026/27 call, the final classification was 60% intermediate classification and 40% interview. The videoconference interview considered motivation, communication, medical knowledge and extracurricular activity.

faq.question: What documents are part of the application?
faq.answer: The call lists identity, academic-access evidence, language evidence and the Group A communication prerequisite. Foreign documents require the stated translation and legalisation route where applicable.

faq.question: What payment is due on enrolment?
faq.answer: The 2026/27 international call states a EUR 100 application fee and a 30% tuition payment of EUR 5,400 at enrolment, plus a registration fee set by Faculty management. The page does not publish a fixed registration amount.

faq.question: Is University accommodation included?
faq.answer: No. University of Lisbon operates student residences, but their availability and monthly fees are separate from Medicine tuition. This package does not represent a residence place as included or guaranteed.

fee.notes: The Faculty's 2026/27 international-Medicine page publishes EUR 18,000 annual tuition. EUR 108,000 is annual tuition multiplied by six years, not a Faculty-published all-in package. The page also lists a EUR 100 application fee, 30% tuition payment at enrolment and a separate registration fee set by Faculty management.

eligibleAudiences: Applicants meeting Portugal's international-student definition with a qualification giving higher-education access in their education system
Applicants holding the relevant Portuguese secondary qualification or equivalent
restrictions: EU citizens and specified EU or Portuguese family, resident, rights-equality and mobility categories are excluded from this international route
The academic areas are Biology, Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics
Portuguese or English B1 entry evidence applies; Portuguese study is required by the end of third year when Portuguese B1 is not held
The cited 2026/27 application timetable is cycle-specific
audienceEligibility.notes: The Faculty published 13 Medicine places at the time the 2026/27 page was checked; second-phase availability depends on first-phase outcomes.

admissionsContent.overview: The verified 2026/27 international route used the Faculty's Fenix application portal. Applicants supplied academic, identity, language and communication-prerequisite evidence, then received an academic review and, where eligible, a videoconference interview.

eligibility.intro: Applicants need an accepted secondary-level access qualification, the required international-student status, relevant science preparation and Portuguese or English B1 evidence.
items: Qualification granting higher-education access in the home education system
Biology, Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics preparation
Portuguese or English B1 evidence, subject to the published exemptions
Group A personal communication prerequisite assessed by a physician registered with the Portuguese Medical Order

applicationSteps: Submit the Medicine application through the Faculty Fenix portal in the published phase
Upload identity, academic-access, language and Group A prerequisite evidence
Provide translation and legalisation documents where the call requires them
Attend the videoconference interview if invited after the academic review
Complete pre-enrolment, registration and the published initial tuition payment after an offer

academic: Academic record and translations where applicable
Portuguese or English B1 evidence where required

admissionsContent.deadlinesNote: For the 2026/27 second phase, applications ran 6 April to 22 May 2026; ranking was due by 12 June, interviews 22–26 June, results by 30 June and pre-enrolment by 3 July. A later cycle requires a new Faculty call.
visaConsiderations: Non-EU applicants need the acceptance documentation and immigration process applicable to their personal status; the University publishes practical visa information separately.

evidence.claimText: For 2026/27, the Faculty's international-Medicine page publishes EUR 18,000 annual tuition, a EUR 100 application fee and a 30% tuition payment at enrolment; the registration fee is set separately by Faculty management.

The 2026/27 international route required academic-access, identity, language and Group A communication-prerequisite evidence, followed by academic ranking and a videoconference interview where invited.

For the 2026/27 second phase, applications ran 6 April to 22 May 2026, interviews were held 22–26 June, results were due by 30 June and pre-enrolment was due by 3 July. The programme is packaged for the September academic-year intake.
The international route accepts Portuguese or English B1 entry evidence. Applicants without Portuguese B1 must complete the stated Portuguese course by the end of the third year.
University of Lisbon publishes student halls of residence with monthly charges set annually; availability and a room assignment are separate from the Faculty's Medicine tuition.
